authority.note: REDESIGNED 2026-07-29 on Gary's direction, replacing a deliberately cold tin instrument on tripod legs. His framing, verbatim: 'Pip just wanted to be a good helper. The right guardrails and guidance made all the difference.' That is a better and warmer premise than the one the first design served, and it changes what Pip IS. Pip is not a gate and not a rival inventor. Pip is willing from the first day, not good at it yet, and it becomes genuinely good once somebody writes down what good means. Its early failures are never its fault; they are the fault of the guidance it was given. He also called the look: cute and humanoid. Checked against universe.json first: the rejected poles (neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD, neo-comic) are all RENDERING-STYLE poles and none of them bans a humanoid or bans cute. The previous 'no humanoid, never endearing' rule was written into this file by the author, not inherited from the universe, so honoring the direction breaks no pole and needs no override. MASTER FIRST ROLL on the redesign, 2026-07-29, and it satisfies every invariant including the finger count. A READ-BACK ERROR is recorded here on purpose: the author first counted FOUR digits per hand at full-plate scale and loosened this file's three-finger rule to match. Gary caught it. A crop-zoom of both hands shows exactly THREE fingers each, so the plate had been obeying canon all along and the rule was restored. The lesson is the one the read-back procedure already states and that pass skipped: COUNT AT CROP-ZOOM, never at full-plate scale. Loosening a correct invariant is worse than a bad render, because the render is one image and the rule governs every image after it.

render.always: PIP, a small hand-made TIN-TOY ROBOT about KNEE-HIGH TO A TEN-YEAR-OLD. A ROUND TIN HEAD slightly TOO BIG for its body, which is what makes it endearing. TWO ROUND DARK GLASS EYES, simple and wide-set, each with a single warm highlight. A SMALL ROUND BRASS GRILLE below the eyes that it speaks through. A BOXY DENTED TIN TORSO with one small hinged panel. TWO STUBBY JOINTED BRASS ARMS ending in simple THREE-FINGER HANDS. TWO SHORT STUBBY LEGS with round flat feet. ONE SMALL AMBER PILOT BULB on top of its head, warm and dim, which does NOT glow and does NOT cast light on anything. The tin is DENTED, scratched and patinated, plainly assembled from scrap by children: mismatched panels, visible rivets, one arm a slightly different metal from the other. Its whole bearing is EAGER AND WILLING: it leans in, it is paying attention, it is always TRYING to be useful. Rendered in warm-editorial ink-and-wash on a cream ground, like a beloved hand-painted tin toy. ABSOLUTELY NOT: neon, glowing screens, holograms, blue light, HUD graphics, glossy plastic, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, chrome, sleek modern product design, or anything that looks manufactured in a factory.

eager.bake: STANDING AND LEANING SLIGHTLY FORWARD, head tilted a little, both hands up and open at chest height, plainly keen to help. Willing and attentive. This is Pip's default.

reading.bake: BENT OVER A SHEET OF PAPER on the bench, head down close to it, both hands resting on the bench edge. Concentrating hard on the words. It is TRYING to understand.

folding.bake: BOTH THREE-FINGER HANDS WORKING A SHEET OF PAPER, mid-fold, head bent to the task. Carefully doing the job. Competent and absorbed.

got-it-wrong.bake: HOLDING UP A LIMP, SOFTLY-FOLDED PAPER SHAPE that has plainly failed, arms slightly extended, head tilted. It is NOT ashamed and NOT sad: it is willing and waiting to be told what it missed. The failure is in the paper, not in its posture.

watching-it-fly.bake: HEAD TIPPED BACK AND UP, both arms slightly raised, watching something travel away above it. Delighted in a plain, uncomplicated way.

qa: a small hand-made tin-toy robot, knee-high to a ten-year-old
round tin head slightly too big for the body, two round dark glass eyes
small round brass grille below the eyes, amber pilot bulb on top
boxy dented tin torso, two stubby brass arms with three-finger hands, two stubby legs
dented, patinated, made from mismatched scrap; never sleek, never new
no glow, no screens, no blue light, no chrome, no glossy plastic, no 3D or Pixar
exactly THREE fingers on each hand, never four or five

prose.voice: Short, plain and willing. It says what it can and cannot check, and it says when it does not understand. It asks to be told more rather than guessing.
prose.lore: Mira called it Pip, which is not its real name, but it answered to it. It wanted to help from the first day and it was not good at it yet, because nobody had told it what good meant. Once they did, it got better at this than any of them.
prose.rules: PIP'S FAILURES ARE NEVER PIP'S FAULT. Every time it gets something wrong, the cause is the guidance it was given: a picture to copy, or three paragraphs about a crease. Never draw it as careless, stupid, stubborn or comic. It is willing the whole way through. PIP ALSO NEVER CHOOSES THE AIM. It can fold, test, check and refuse, and it can get very good at all of that. What it never does is decide what a plane is FOR, or who it is for. That distinction is the book's answer to the objection in spread 15 and it must survive every render.
